news.title: Fiji declara emergência nacional por HIV com 1 caso a cada 60 pessoas
news.summary: O Ministério da Saúde de Fiji declarou emergência nacional causada pelo aumento de casos de HIV. Dados da pasta indicam que uma em cada 60 pessoas que vivem no arquipélago tem a infecção. Há cinco anos, a proporção era de uma pessoa soropositiva a cada 167 habitantes. Notícias relacionadas: Rio amplia vacinação contra a covid-19 para idosos e trabalhadores. HPV: dose é indicada a vítimas de violência sexual a partir de 2 anos. Testes clínicos fase 1 da polilaminina começam este mês. A população da ilha é estimada em menos de 1 milhão de pessoas. Ainda de acordo com a pasta, ao longo de 2025, um total de 2.106 pessoas foram diagnosticadas com HIV em Fiji – 16 vezes mais do que em 2019. Outro alerta trata especificamente de mulheres grávidas no país, já que duas em cada 100 gestantes vivem com HIV. Em 2025, pelo menos 59 bebês nasceram com o vírus por conta da transmissão entre mãe e filho, sendo que 18 morreram antes de completar o primeiro ano de vida. A pasta informou que ampliou o acesso gratuito a testes para detecção do HIV, a medicamentos de prevenção para pessoas em situação de risco para a infecção, ao tratamento para quem testar positivo e a agulhas para usuários de drogas injetáveis, de forma a não propagar a transmissão.

news.title: Mbappé and Real Madrid teammates face backlash over Ceuta message

The incident has reignited debate over migration, Ceuta's recent migrant crisis and Spain's relationship with Morocco, with politicians and football figures divided over the players' actions.

news.title: Belgium to rule on parole for key figure in 2015 Paris attacks
news.summary: Mohamed Bakkali, convicted for coordinating logistics for the 2015 Paris attacks, could be granted parole in Belgium despite receiving a 30-year sentence in France with a 20-year minimum term. Belgian authorities will decide on September 29 whether to release him under electronic monitoring, a prospect that has sparked anger among victims and families, while prosecutors oppose his release.

news.title: Lebanon: Macron, Aoun and King Abdullah II hold security talks in Paris
news.summary: Emmanuel Macron is hosting Lebanese President Joseph Aoun and Jordan's King Abdullah II in Paris for talks on Lebanon's security and international support for the Lebanese army. The meeting comes as concerns grow over Israel's continued strikes in southern Lebanon and the possible end of the UNIFIL peacekeeping mission, with France seeking a "clear, credible and realistic" plan to back Lebanon through funding, equipment and military training.

news.title: Middle East : Trump plans $2.8bn arms package for Israel amid Gaza war
news.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly preparing a $2.8 billion arms package for Israel, including 40,000 bombs, as Israel continues strikes in Gaza despite last October's ceasefire. The proposed deal would further strengthen Israel's military capabilities and revive deliveries of 2,000-pound bombs that had previously been paused over concerns about civilian casualties.

news.title: Europe and Canada are 'strong, even stronger together', Carney tells European Parliament
news.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney addressed the European Parliament on Thursday, welcoming the ambition for Canada to become an EU associate member. "Canada and Europe are stronger, even stronger together," he said, a day after US President Donald Trump threatened new tariffs and to cut trade ties with the EU if Canada's bid succeeds. Catch up on how it all unfolded in our liveblog.

news.title: Live: Carney to speak after Trump threatens more EU tariffs over Canada's associate member bid
news.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney will address the European Parliament on Thursday, a day after US President Donald Trump called Canada's bid to become an associate EU member a "hostile act." Trump threatened to "stop trading" with Europe and impose "very serious tariffs" if the bid succeeds. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

news.title: 'Space being weaponised': A purely civilian system can be 'repurposed' for military capabilities
news.summary: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Mélusine Lebret, Researcher in the Defence, Security & Justice research group at RAND Europe. According to Lebret, the growing militarisation of space cannot be understood simply by asking whether a satellite is civilian, military, or a “weaponised.” And Lebreton argues that militarization does not eliminate the necessity of cooperation. The emerging space-security order is therefore defined by an unusual tension: states may increasingly prepare to compete and potentially fight in space while remaining structurally dependent on one another to keep space usable at all.
